Coram : Gautam A. Ankhad, J.
 Date : 17Th October 2025.
The Applicant have filed this Arbitration Application under Section 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 ("the Act") seeking appointment of a Sole Arbitrator.

Mr. Sarang Pathak,
learned counsel for the Applicants states that the Applicants have entered into Franchise Agreement, Content Agreement and Franchise Food Business & Safety Agreement, all dated 13 th October 2020.

It is the Applicants' case that the documents were executed and when the breaches were brought to the notice of the Respondents, the Respondents wrongfully terminated the above Agreements on 1 st December 2023.
In the termination notice it is wrongly alleged that the said contracts were signed under pressure.
Mr. Pathak submits that there was no pressure whatsoever and the disputes have only been raised years later by the Respondents.
On account of non-payment of the dues under these Agreements, correspondence was exchanged and finally on 15th January 2024, the Applicants invoked arbitration under the aforesaid three Agreements.

The Respondents have, in reply, falsely denied the said arbitration Digitally signed by ABHAY DIXIT ABHAY Date:
7-ARBAP(L)-19110-2024.doc Dixit DIXIT 2025.10.17 18:51:12 +0530 contract.
It is in this background that the present Application is filed.
Mr. Pathak, learned counsel tenders an affidavit-of-service dated 12 th August 2025.
He submits that the service has been refused deliberately to avoid this Application.
2. I have perused the record.

It is settled law as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in K. Bhaskaran v. Sankaran Vaidhyan Balan & Anr., (1999) 7 SCC 510, that when a party refuses the service, it is deemed to be valid service in law.

Krish Spinning, (2025) 3 SCC (Civ) 567 that the Section 11 Court ought not to venture beyond examining the existence of an arbitration agreement.

Being satisfied that an arbitration agreement is in existence and that the arbitration has been duly invoked, I refer all disputes and differences between the parties under the above Agreements to arbitration by a Sole Arbitrator.

In these circumstances, the Arbitration Application (Lodging)
No.19110 of 2024 is disposed of in the following terms :-

Mr. Rohan Kelkar, Advocate, is hereby appointed as the Sole Arbitrator to adjudicate upon the disputes and differences between the parties arising out of and in connection with the Agreements referred to above.

The contact details of Mr. Rohan Kelkar, the Sole Arbitrator, are "Off.Add. : 14-C, Examiner Press Building, Dalal Street, Fort, Mumbai - 400001, Mobile No.:9820446842, E-mail :
kelkar.rohanegmail.com".

[B]. A copy of this order will be communicated to the learned Sole Arbitrator by the Advocate for the Applicants within a period of one week from the date on which this order is uploaded on the website of this Court.
The Applicants shall provide the contact and communication particulars of the parties to the Arbitral Tribunal along with a copy of this order;

[C]. The learned Sole Arbitrator is requested to forward the statutory Statement of Disclosure under Section 11(8) read with Section 12(1) of the Act to the Advocate for the 7-ARBAP(L)-19110-2024.doc Dixit Applicant so as to enable them to file the same in the Registry of this Court.
The Registry of this Court shall retain the said Statement on the file of this Arbitration Application and a copy of the same shall be furnished by the Advocate for the Applicants to the Respondents;
